A 27-year-old G1P0 at 12 weeks estimated gestational age presents for prenatal care. The patient says she has occasional nausea and vomiting and a few episodes of palpitations and diarrhea this last week. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for a heart rate of 145/min. Basic thyroid function tests are shown in the table below. Which of the following additional laboratory tests would be most useful is assessing this patient’s condition?
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) 
0.28 mIU/L (0.3–4.5 mIU/L)
Total T4
12 µg/dL (5.4–11.5 µg/dL)?

                    ### Question
                    A 27-year-old G1P0 at 12 weeks estimated gestational age presents for prenatal care. The patient says she has occasional nausea and vomiting and a few episodes of palpitations and diarrhea this last week. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for a heart rate of 145/min. Basic thyroid function tests are shown in the table below. Which of the following additional laboratory tests would be most useful is assessing this patient’s condition?
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) 
0.28 mIU/L (0.3–4.5 mIU/L)
Total T4
12 µg/dL (5.4–11.5 µg/dL)?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Total triiodothyronine (T3) levels
opb. Free thyroxine (T4) levels
opc. Thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) levels
opd. Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies
ope. Thyrotropin receptor antibodies (TRAb)

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with symptoms and lab findings suggestive of hyperthyroidism, characterized by low TSH and elevated Total T4. In pregnancy, it is crucial to differentiate between true hyperthyroidism and physiological changes. The most direct and consensus-aligned approach is to assess Free T4 levels, as Total T4 can be elevated due to increased Thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) during pregnancy. Free T4 provides a clearer picture of thyroid function. While Thyrotropin receptor antibodies (TRAb) can help diagnose Graves' disease, Free T4 is more immediately useful in confirming hyperthyroidism. The retrieved evidence paths highlight the association of hyperthyroidism with triiodothyronine (T3), but Free T4 remains the primary test to confirm hyperthyroidism in this context. Therefore, the most useful additional laboratory test is Free T4 levels.
